newsitem.title: USA: May posts stronger results, plans 13 new stores in 1997.
newsitem.headline: May posts stronger results, plans 13 new stores in 1997.

text.p: May Department Stores Co. Wednesday reported higher fourth-quarter and full-year earnings, raised its quarterly dividend and said it plans to open 13 new stores in 1997.
May attributed its strong performance to the spin-off of Payless ShoeSource Inc., a shoe retailer, allowing it to focus entirely on department stores.

"We continued to add value for the customer by enhancing our stores' positions in key designers and brands, broadening our merchandise selections and improving our private labels," Chairman David Farrell said in a statement.
May's profits rose to $418 million, or $1.59 a share, in the quarter ended Feb. 1, including a loss of $5 million for early retirement of debt.
In the 1995 period, earnings were $362 million, or $1.36 a share, including losses of $34 million from discontinued operations and early debt retirement.
Revenues rose 10.5 percent to $4.0 billion from $3.6 billion.
Full-year earnings rose to $755 million, or $2.84 a share, from $752 million, or $2.81 a share, in 1995. Revenues rose 11 percent to a record $11.7 billion from $10.5 billion.
May also raised its quarterly dividend to 30 cents a share from 29 cents, effective with the March 15 payment for holders of record as of March 1.
In 1996, May opened 15 department stores and acquired 13, bringing its retail network to 365 stores in 30 states and Washington, D.C. as of Feb. 1.

"We acquired 13 Strawbridge's stores in 1996, strengthening our position in Philadelphia," said Farrell. "We now have 21 Strawbridge's stores in the greater Philadelphia area, which are operated by Hecht's, our largest department store division."
In addition, the retailer said it will repurchase up to $300 million of its shares, on top of the $600 million repurchase programme completed in January.
May stock fell 50 cents to $47 on the New York Stock Exchange.
